HMW-V24

"How might we connect a driver to their assigned FM job via WeChat — so the dispatcher can hand off job details instantly after assignment, without WhatsApp copy-paste?"
Gap in the current flow: TODO-048 (driver assignment — shipped) lets a dispatcher select Zhang Wei + 粤B·12345 in Teleport OS. But after pressing Assign, there is no mechanism to tell the driver. In practice, dispatchers screenshot the job detail, paste into a WeChat group, or read the address aloud. The WeChat Mini Program (HMW-V09) is designed but not yet built. This HMW explores how the assignment event bridges to the driver's WeChat experience. Three meaningfully different options: (A) QR code deep-link generated at assignment time, (B) WeChat subscription/template message sent to driver's WeChat ID, (C) Driver pulls their own jobs list in the mini program each morning. Each option has different integration requirements and driver UX implications.

Option A — QR Code at Assignment (Zero Integration)

Option A
When the dispatcher assigns a driver + vehicle in Teleport OS, a QR code immediately appears below the assigned driver in the Dispatch Assignment section. The QR encodes a deep link to the WeChat mini program for that specific job (e.g., pages/job/detail?tripId=DO-001&jobId=J04). Driver scans with WeChat's built-in QR scanner → mini program opens to the exact job. The QR code is also included in the printable Job Sheet (HMW-V21, which reserves a slot for this exact purpose). The dispatcher does not need to copy text or describe the address — the QR is the handoff artifact.

Pros
• Zero WeChat developer overhead — no subscription template approval
• Works offline (QR can be printed on job sheet)
• QR slot already reserved in HMW-V21 print-preview
• Clear physical handoff artifact: dispatcher holds phone, driver scans
• If driver loses the link, dispatcher regenerates from the same screen
Cons
• Requires driver to be physically close (or dispatcher screenshot → WeChat)
• QR must be regenerated if job is reassigned to different driver
• Driver has no push notification — must scan to know they're assigned
• WeChat mini program must be built first (QR is useless without it)

Option B — WeChat Template Message (Push Notification)

Option B
When the dispatcher assigns a driver in Teleport OS, the system sends a WeChat template/subscription message to the driver's registered WeChat ID (stored in the Driver master data: Driver.wechatId). The message contains: job ID, pickup location, pickup time, cargo summary, and a deep-link to open the mini program. The driver taps the card in their WeChat message list → mini program opens directly to the job. No dispatcher action beyond the normal assignment.

Pros
• Instant — driver is notified the moment dispatcher assigns
• No dispatcher action after assignment (notification is automatic)
• Deep-links directly to the job in mini program
• Driver receives assignment notification even if not at warehouse
Cons
• Requires WeChat developer account + subscription message template approval (24-48h review, requires official entity registration)
• Driver must follow the Teleport OS service account to receive messages
• Template message content is heavily regulated — format constraints
• If WeChat ID is wrong/outdated in fleet data, notification fails silently
• High regulatory friction for prototype stage

Option C — Driver Pulls Own Jobs in Mini Program (No Notification)

Option C
No push mechanism at all. Drivers open the Teleport OS WeChat mini program each day, authenticate by phone number (their number on file in the Driver master data), and see all jobs assigned to them. The mini program home screen is a date-sorted job list filtered to that driver. Driver navigates to their job from the list. Dispatcher tells the driver "check your Teleport app" via existing channels (WeChat, phone). This requires the fewest integrations — just the mini program with a driver auth flow.

Pros
• Fewest integrations — mini program auth only (phone number)
• Driver has full daily job overview in one screen
• Works even if WeChat ID data is missing
• Driver can check upcoming jobs and plan the day
• No WeChat platform approval needed beyond mini program itself
Cons
• Driver must proactively open the app to learn about assignments
• Relies on dispatcher to verbally tell driver "check the app"
• Misses the WeChat-native notification workflow drivers already use
• Driver may miss re-assignments or cancellations without checking
• Adds friction to the handoff vs. existing WhatsApp group message

Recommendation: Option A (QR Code) for v1 — Option B (Push) for v1.1

Ship QR first. Option A requires no WeChat platform registration beyond the mini program itself. The QR code slot is already reserved in HMW-V21's print-preview job sheet. Implementation cost: generate the mini program deep link URL when a driver is assigned and render it as a QR in the Dispatch Assignment section. The dispatcher taps "Copy link" to forward via WeChat if not physically co-located. Zero new infrastructure.

Plan subscription messages for v1.1. Option B is the correct long-term UX — drivers are already conditioned to act on WeChat template messages from logistics platforms. Start the WeChat service account application and subscription message template approval in parallel with v1 shipping. Approval takes 2-4 weeks. Wire it up in v1.1 once approved. Both A and B can coexist: the QR stays as a fallback if the driver hasn't subscribed.

Reject Option C as default. Pure pull is insufficient because drivers miss re-assignments and cancellations. Option C works only as a supplement to A or B — the daily job overview screen is valuable, but it cannot be the sole notification mechanism in a time-sensitive dispatch workflow.

Open question for user: Does the WeChat mini program authenticate drivers by (a) phone number match against fleet data, (b) WeChat OAuth (driver authorizes with their WeChat account), or (c) vendor code + driver name? Option (b) is most reliable (phone numbers change; WeChat ID is persistent) but requires more OAuth scope approval. Recommend (b) for v1.1, (a) for the v1 QR fallback.
